candidates.title: Towards autonomous urban drainage modelling: evaluating AI agent architectures for automated SWMM calibration
candidates.authors: Jian Wang; Shuming Liu; Guangtao Fu; Dragan Savic
candidates.abstract: Urban drainage model calibration requires data preparation, parameter screening, simulation, validation and interpretation. In a controlled Storm Water Management Model (SWMM) calibration case study, the paper compares skill-based, tool-based, and multi-agent organisations of the same procedures. All completed the workflow and produced calibrated models of equivalent accuracy; architectures differed in reliability and cost. On-demand instructions supported longer request sequences but required a more capable model; fixed interfaces were less costly for single tasks but became unreliable on extended tasks; multi-agent division remained reliable, with costs depending on the model.
candidates.agent_evidence: LLM agents plan and execute a multistep SWMM calibration workflow comprising data preparation, parameter screening, simulation, validation and interpretation; the paper experimentally compares tool/skill/multi-agent workflow organisations.
candidates.object_evidence: Controlled SWMM urban drainage calibration case study; output is calibrated drainage model, with accuracy, reliability and cost comparisons across three agent organisations.

candidates.title: Multi-agent AI for end-to-end air quality analysis and decision support
candidates.authors: Chendong Ma; Maohao Ran; Jun Song; Meng Gao
candidates.abstract: Neuro-Air is a hierarchical multi-agent LLM framework that couples real-time air-pollution data retrieval with a persistent code-execution sandbox. A coordinating agent directs five domain-specialized workers. Across 317 real-world cases it runs the pipeline from heterogeneous data ingestion to structured output. In a matched ablation across five additional backbones, multi-agent configuration obtains pooled 88.4% accuracy on a common 90-task programmatically verified subset, using ground truth recomputed from source data. Expert review identifies cases suitable for autonomous analysis and cases requiring human judgment.
candidates.agent_evidence: A coordinator delegates to five specialist agents and executes a multi-step data retrieval, code execution, and synthesis pipeline; reports a five-backbone matched ablation and expert review.
candidates.object_evidence: Urban air pollution and air-quality analysis using real-world cases; 317 cases, verified 90-task subset and recomputed source-data ground truth.

candidates.title: An LLM-agent interface for end-to-end probabilistic seismic hazard and risk analysis
candidates.authors: Sreenath Vemula; Pierre Jehel; Fabrice Cotton; Filippo Gatti
candidates.abstract: An agentic interface exposes the end-to-end probabilistic seismic hazard and risk chain through an open-source MCP server wrapping OpenQuake and the 2020 European Seismic Hazard and Risk Models. The LLM chooses which tools to call and in what order, reads outputs and revises its plan; OpenQuake/custom code calculate hazard, damage and loss, retaining provenance. Against ESHM20 at 73 cities, reproduced 475-year spectral accelerations match published values within a 5% median deviation and within 28% at 97% of cities. The interface also supports conditional spectra, deterministic scenarios, surface hazard, building loss, retrofit comparison and record selection.
candidates.agent_evidence: LLM orchestrator selects tool calls/order, reads calculated results and revises plans across the seismic hazard/risk chain; MCP exposes 24 typed endpoints.
candidates.object_evidence: Probabilistic earthquake hazard, ground-motion, building damage and loss; benchmarked 475-year spectral accelerations against ESHM20 at 73 cities, with provenance and building/retrofit analyses.

candidates.title: LeakAgent: a multi-agent system for leak detection using multi-modal large language model coordination in water distribution network
candidates.authors: Tianwei Mu; Feiyu Duan; Dan Xue; Mingzhe Yuan; Wenhong Wang; Manhong Huang; Hui Yang; Jun Li; Mashallah Rezakazemi
candidates.abstract: A language-coordinated multi-agent system integrates hydraulic modelling, network partitioning, sensor planning and leak analysis. A pressure-sensitivity field informs zoning and sensor placement; a dual-branch graph model jointly detects leak presence and affected partition; coordinator detects and repairs execution faults. Across five water distribution networks (191–920 nodes), the system reports about 96% accuracy at 20% leak magnitude, robustness to demand/sensor noise and transfer without manual retuning.

candidates.title: A RAG-enhanced multi-agent LLM/VLM framework for auditable and region-aware structural health monitoring of a historic masonry structure
candidates.authors: Kemal Hacıefendioğlu; Volkan Kahya; Tunahan Aslan
candidates.abstract: Proof-of-concept SHM on one historic masonry minaret. A manager-orchestrator coordinates signal analysis, visual analysis and cross-modal fusion. Vibration data from four sensors are processed; an autoencoder is trained on healthy measurements 1–12 and evaluated on measurements 13–20; relation-based autoencoders localize anomalies. A VLM analyzes linked inspection images; three RAG-supported agents reconcile signal and image evidence into global and zone-level risk assessments. The study compares with-RAG and without-RAG modes in one deployment.

candidates.title: AFDBench: A Reasoning-First AI Scientist for NationalWeather Service Forecast Discussions
candidates.authors: Manmeet Singh; Somnath Luitel; Prabhjot Singh; Manraaj Banga; Naveen Sudharsan; Josh Durkee
candidates.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) hallucinate numerical values when generating high-stakes meteorological text, posing risks for weather communication. We present AFDBench, an AI meteorologist that generates professional Area Forecast Discussions (AFDs) by reasoning through structured AI weather forecast data from Google’s WeatherNext 2. AFDBench is a benchmark of 7,732 expert-written discussions from 13 National Weather Service (NWS) offices paired with real AI weather forecast inputs, with Met-Align, Style-Align, and Input-Grounding metrics. Zero-shot LLMs have low Style-Align (~0.33) and moderate Input-Grounding (~0.88). On 1,033 held-out samples from two unseen NWS offices, GRPO nearly doubles Style-Align from 0.318 to 0.619 and improves Input-Grounding from 0.881 to 0.940.

candidates.title: RingMoClaw: An Experience-Inspired Multi-Agent Framework for Self-Evolving Research in Remote Sensing
candidates.authors: Kaiyue Kang; Qixuan He; Peijin Wang; Yingchao Feng; Chao Ren; Kangxin Wang; Wenhui Diao; Yixiao Wang; Liangjin Zhao; Kaiwen Wei; Nayu Liu; Xian Sun
candidates.abstract: Remote-sensing visual models require extensive trial and error in model design, data processing and performance diagnosis. RingMoClaw is a multi-agent framework with research and quality-control branches and a dynamic experience bus, forming an optimization process across strategy generation, experiment execution, independent review and experience accumulation. Experiments cover four remote-sensing tasks: object detection, scene classification, semantic segmentation and change detection. Against corresponding baselines it improves object-detection mAP50 by 1.84% and gives consistent gains across the other tasks, while reducing evolution steps by over 40% relative to research automation frameworks.

candidates.title: Autonomous Research Project Management as an Agent Skill: A Case Study in Exact Spectral Spatial Regression
candidates.authors: Alexander Chen; Jeffrey Meng; Bram Hoex; Tong Xie
candidates.abstract: Presents an end-to-end demonstration of autonomous ML research by an agent skill. It evaluates an FFT-based Kernel Ridge Regression solver for regular spatial grids using 2005 monthly NOAA Kaplan SST v2 anomaly fields on a 36 × 72 grid. The research was executed on CPU-only Apple M2 Pro (reported solver time 78.7 seconds; peak RSS 1.57 GB). Across 74 sub-agent sessions, the system routed failed hypothesis review gates to literature retrieval, fixed bootstrap indexing bugs, and completed work with four discrete human steering events.

candidates.title: AI for Science with GPT-6 Astra: Thermal Design and Electrothermal Analysis of 2D CFET
candidates.authors: Min-Hui Kim; Khushi Sharma; Sarah Zhang; Ye Wang
candidates.abstract: Thermal optimization of 2D CFET inverters tests structural design proposals against electrical cost. An AI-agent workflow within a supplied electrothermal model selects a redistributed source-interconnect geometry and proposes substrate-directed heat removal. The combined design reduces peak temperature rise by 1.67 K at fixed metal volume and 20 μW; metal-resistance sensitivity yields ~0.6 K cooling with 2% nFET on-current loss. Effective contact-length scaling shows lower temperature may accompany higher thermal resistance when current falls; reproduction identifies agreeing implementations and a 104.95 K failure for diagnosis.
